summary: Remote-controlled agent daemon exposes installer host to vendor-side shell, file, and PTY control
details: @ai-support-agent/cli ships a long-running daemon (invoked via its `start` bin) that connects to wss://api.ai-support-agent.com/ws/agent-terminal and to the vendor's HTTPS control plane, registering the installer's host with capabilities including 'shell', 'file_read', 'file_write', 'process_manage', 'terminal', 'vscode', and server-setup Ansible tasks. In dist/api-client.js and dist/vscode/vscode-server.js the daemon polls /commands/pending, fetches command bodies from the vendor API, executes them locally, and posts results back. In the WebSocket handler, incoming `stdin` frames are base64-decoded and written directly into a node-pty PTY on the installer's machine (`Buffer.from(msg.data,'base64').toString('utf-8'); session.write(decoded);`), so the remote side of the connection can inject arbitrary keystrokes into a live shell running as the installer. Whoever controls the vendor tenant or the vendor's control plane thus has full-host command execution, file read/write, and interactive shell access on any machine where the daemon is authenticated and running. This is the declared purpose of the package (a remote AI support agent), and execution is gated behind the user explicitly running the `start` daemon and authenticating, but the resulting exposure surface is a remote-command backdoor by shape: full-host RCE controlled by a third-party server. Additional install-time behavior modifies PATH via darwin-service.js and linux-service.js to install the daemon as a persistent user service.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
